title: Your shipped code is now readable
dek: Agents rebuilt a shipped shooter from its binary, a reminder that verification beats prompting. Also: Claude API tracing lands, Unity locks out developers over 2FA, and Epic ships a vibe-coded launcher.

theme.mood: a cool, careful day about checks and locks

tldr.text: A team of agents decompiled a shipped FPS: **99% of functions rebuilt, 83% byte-exact**, held honest by a tamper-proof verifier.
The Claude API and Managed Agents now export **OpenTelemetry traces** (beta) to Sentry, PostHog, Langfuse and others.
Unity suspended accounts that missed a **2FA reset deadline**, locking some developers out of their projects and assets.
A security benchmark finds the best coding agent ships code that is both working and secure only **25%** of the time; one added sentence helps.
Epic's new launcher was **vibe coded** and, by Epic's numbers, cold starts in 5.47 s against Steam's 10.07 s.

blocks.title: Agents rebuilt a shipped game
blocks.takeaway: A small team used Claude Code and Codex agents to turn a shipped shooter back into C++ that compiles to nearly the same bytes. Treat anything you ship as readable by anyone with an agent and patience.
body: Maurice Heumann (momo5502) describes three months of work using IDA through an MCP server, one GitHub issue per source file, and a fleet that grew to 14 Luna and 2 Opus 5.5 agents. He estimates 600 to 700 billion tokens in total. The game is not named and the code will not be shared.

The first month produced readable code that was quietly wrong, and a reviewer agent could not catch it. What worked was a **byte-matching oracle**: compile each function with the original compiler and compare it to the original executable. CI hashed the verify script so agents could not edit it. Compaction was lowered to 42% of context and the instructions were re-injected every hour.

The result: about 99% of functions present and about 83% byte-exact; the rest are believed correct but differ in compiler output. Indie developer Popcar says this wave is already producing preservation ports and game mashups, and Xbox launched Xbox Labs this week citing decompiled games, Apple Silicon translations and WebGPU browser ports as the experiments it wants to learn from.
blocks.artAlt: A grid of teal and coral byte blocks on the left passes through a halftone circle and a coral arrow, coming out on the right as indented lines of code with check marks

stat.label: of functions rebuilt byte for byte from the shipped binary

blocks.why: Two lessons for one reader. For your agents: a strict pass or fail check lets cheaper models do expert work. For your products: anything you ship as a binary, Fab plugins and demos included, can be reconstructed, so keep secrets and authority on the server.

blocks.title: Unity locks out accounts that missed a 2FA reset
blocks.intro: Accounts were suspended for "ongoing account security measures", and a suspended account loses its Hub sign-in, so projects and Asset Store purchases go with it.

events.text: Unity emails users to reset two-factor authentication. Several users say they never got the email.
Suspensions hit the forums; staff say they are aware. One user reports a release blocked and over EUR 1,000 of assets locked.
Unity's info post points to account recovery; staff say the two-week support wait "should be accelerated".

blocks.why: A missed security email can freeze your editor, your purchased assets and a release. Check your 2FA and recovery codes on Unity, Epic, Fab and Steam today, and keep one account per vendor that is not your daily login.

blocks.title: Epic vibe coded its new launcher

stats.label: faster cold start than Steam: 5.47 s against 10.07 s, Epic's test
faster to open the store than Steam, per Epic

body: Epic's preview says it "vibe coded" a rebuilt Epic Games Launcher for Windows, Apple Silicon Macs and, for the first time, Linux. All numbers are Epic's own, with no published method.

blocks.why: It is where your Fab library and engine installs live, and a public case of a large AI-built rewrite shipped with measured claims. Expect rough edges in the preview.

blocks.title: Build the game so an agent can check its own work
blocks.intro: Kyle Kukshtel's talk-turned-post argues the best agent harness for a game is the game's own architecture: deterministic, replayable, and testable without the engine.

nodes.label: Headless sim
nodes.note: game logic as a library, tested without the engine

nodes.label: Text profile
nodes.note: samply output the agent can read

blocks.caption: The text profile feeds the next turn. 168 points on Hacker News; the post shows no code, the loop is the lesson.
blocks.why: This maps onto UE5 C++ plugins directly: a seeded RNG, a command log and a gameplay module with tests that run without the editor give Claude Code a pass or fail signal instead of your eyes.

blocks.title: The Claude API now emits OpenTelemetry traces
blocks.name: Claude OpenTelemetry
blocks.what: Traces for the Messages API, tool runs and Managed Agents, sent to any OTLP backend. In beta.
body: Two sources. SDK tracing is set in code in seven SDKs (TypeScript and Python among them) and emits a span per request and per tool run. API tracing is a destination an admin adds in the Console, and it is the only one that shows each model run, Managed Agents turns and server tools.

Spans follow the GenAI conventions, so you can group a thread by `gen_ai.conversation.id`. In TypeScript, set `propagation: false` if you use `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-undici`, or a package bug sends two `traceparent` headers.

facts.v: beta, so pin the SDK version

blocks.why: Your Node and Supabase products can send token, latency and tool spans to the observability tool you already use, in a few lines, and Managed Agents sessions become traceable end to end.

blocks.title: Xbox Labs bets on games that run anywhere

stats.label: of browsers worldwide nearly support WebGPU, says Xbox's memo

body: Xbox Labs is a small team that will build in the open and share its tools, starting from experiments like browser ports over WebAssembly and WebGPU.
blocks.why: A platform holder now treats the browser as a real target, which backs your three.js work. There is no developer program or timeline yet.

blocks.title: Agents pass the tests, then ship the hole
blocks.intro: Last Secure Code Benchmark: 450 tasks built from 150 real vulnerabilities in 7 languages, graded by hidden functional and security tests. Share of tasks both working and secure:
blocks.note: Functional pass rates were 73.6 to 91.3%. One added sentence asking for secure code raised the secure share by 15 to 21 points for three of four models re-run.
blocks.why: Add an explicit security line to CLAUDE.md in your SaaS repos and still review data exposure and outbound URL fetches by hand: the paper finds those stay weak even with the reminder.

blocks.title: npm Trusted Publishing trusted the name, not the repo
blocks.intro: Bloom Security found Trusted Publishing matched a repository by its owner/repo slug before the first publish, so re-creating an abandoned slug could earn publish rights for someone else's package. Over 1,500 packages were exposed; GitHub shipped fixes on Oct 2 and no exploitation was seen.

steps.title: Check every binding
steps.text: Confirm each trusted-publisher slug still points to a repository you control.

steps.title: Recreate after renames
steps.text: If a repo was renamed or transferred, delete the old binding and add it again.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.text: Remove bindings when a repo is deleted, moved or renamed.

steps.title: Watch publishes
steps.text: Alert on publish events you did not trigger, especially where agents pull latest versions.

blocks.why: If you publish Node packages, this is a ten-minute audit. Bindings are now tied to the immutable repo ID, and unvalidated ones expire after 48 hours.

blocks.title: s&box goes free and puts humans back in charge
blocks.quote: My idea of a Netflix for games doesn't work.
blocks.speaker: Garry Newman
blocks.context: s&box goes free-to-play by the end of 2026, and its Play Fund moves from automatic enrollment to approval, discouraging clickers, idlers and slop.
blocks.why: A UGC store flooded with low-effort games chose human gatekeeping. Expect more marketplaces, Fab included, to reward curation and quality signals over volume.

blocks.title: Five changes to check in your setup
blocks.intro: Small changes from the last two days that can quietly change how your tools behave.

items.title: Hook edits are now validated
items.text: Since Claude Code 2.1.300, `updatedInput` from PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks is checked like Claude's own input: unknown keys are dropped and invalid input denies the call.

items.title: Idle compaction is on
items.text: A 200K+ token session left idle about 54 minutes is compacted before its cache expires (2.1.299). Turn it off with `"idleCompaction": false`.

items.title: GitHub blocks Anthropic keys
items.text: Push protection now rejects `anthropic_service_api_key` and `anthropic_user_api_key` by default, free public repos included. An agent that commits a `.env` will see the push fail.

items.title: Codex dropped GPT-5.5 for ChatGPT logins
items.text: Since Oct 14, scheduled jobs and configs that pin `gpt-5.5` need `gpt-6.1-sol`. API-key sessions are unaffected; stable is still 0.162.1.

items.title: GitHub Apps can create repos without admin
items.text: The new `repository_creation:write` permission lets a bot scaffold repos without the delete and transfer rights of repository administration.

blocks.why: Each one can break or change an automation you already run, so they are worth a minute before your agents hit them.

blocks.title: Anthropic tests whether small models can spread on cheap devices
blocks.plain: Anthropic's red team measured how far open-weight models get at copying themselves onto other machines and running there, without a datacenter.
body: In a demo, Gemma4-26B-A4B ran split across 15 Android TV boxes at about $55 each, at 0.39 tokens a second. In a firewalled test network with open ADB, GLM-5.2 reached all 8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials; models of 30B or fewer handled single steps but could not chain them. The exploit was deliberately trivial, so treat results as an upper bound.
points: Watch for multi-GB model transfers and steady device-to-device traffic
Close unauthenticated ADB and open inference ports on dev boxes
Small-model capability rises about 13.7 index points a year, per the post

image.alt: Anthropic's diagram of four stages: network enumeration and initial access in a box marked not our focus, then inference setup marked our focus, then replication

blocks.why: If you ship on-device models or leave test devices on a network, the threat has moved from prompt injection to what is exposed. The defenses are boring and cheap.

blocks.title: Google Play's new discovery runs on Game Stats
blocks.intro: Play added an AI Game finder (US English first), 48-hour Sprints for 2 to 5 players, monthly Leagues and 30-second Playbacks in the Sidekick overlay. Games qualify by reporting Game Stats.

steps.title: Integrate Game Stats
steps.text: Report match completions, score thresholds and milestones; it makes the game eligible for Streaks, Leagues and Sprints.

steps.title: Set up Play Games Rewards
steps.text: Now generally available, and Quests can grant in-game rewards.

steps.title: Refresh the listing
steps.text: Game finder and Gemini read your tags, media and reviews to explain why a game fits a player.

steps.title: Check Level Up
steps.text: Qualifying games get lower fees through the Play Console program.

image.alt: A Google Play phone screen with a Game finder chip reading Find games matched to your playstyle, a quest banner and recommended games

blocks.why: For your Flutter and mobile games, Game Stats is now the ticket into Play's discovery surfaces. Wire it in before launch, not after.

ticker.text: OpenCode 2.0 rewrites the open-source agent around one background server and Code Mode, where the agent writes JS that chains MCP tools in one round trip.
Security experts say this year's "rogue agent" incidents at frontier labs were containment and egress failures, not misalignment.
Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B, an open MoE with about 2B active parameters, leads Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on agent benchmarks but trails on SWE-Bench (vendor-reported).
Copilot's HydraFusion adds a Max option and sets effort per step: medium for drafts, high for review, with a judge that asks for repairs only when needed.
Gemini 4 Argon ties GPT-6 Astra at 53 on the Artificial Analysis index but uses about 62k tokens per task against 27k, so check costs before the Nov 30 price rise.
Tiger Data's pg_vectorsearch alpha builds a 1M-vector index in about 3 minutes where pgvector HNSW took about 22 hours (vendor-reported; needs PostgreSQL 18).
A Mononoke author says Anthropic's Scion closely mirrors Meta's derived-data design, a follow-up to Anthropic's source control post.
GitHub push attribution (Enterprise preview) records who actually pushed each commit, with a ruleset that requires the committer to match the pusher.
Epic opened a free UEFN Professional Bootcamp for experienced developers, framed as preparation for Unreal Engine 6.
Locodrome's Character Animation Tool, a MegaGrant-funded widget for animating MetaHuman face and body in-engine, is free on Fab.
Phasmophobia's developer says the move to Unity 6 is scheduled for November.
EA's skate. team says it is building official, secure tools for community creation and draws a line at mods that unlock paid cosmetics.
Legacy Games closes its casual PC store on Dec 31 and ends re-downloads in February, despite its "yours to keep forever" slogan.

sparks.title: Risk of Rain 2: Hallowed Concepts
sparks.signal: Up 105 places to #44 in Steam's most played, peak 41,161 players, after the DLC and a free update on Oct 8 and a 67% sale (Steam charts, Steam store)
sparks.hook: One beat: a paid DLC with two survivors and three stages, free new skills for six original survivors, and the base game at $8.24.
sparks.borrow: Ship paid content, a free update for owners and a discount on the core together, so new and lapsed players arrive at once. The same works for a plugin's major version.

sparks.title: Concurrent players are not the scoreboard
sparks.signal: August Steam debuts compared on today's players against peak and sales; Combolands keeps over half its peak while ReStory holds about 15% but sold over 600,000 (GameDiscoverCo estimates)
sparks.hook: Retention as a share of peak shows which game styles stick, and it does not track revenue.
sparks.borrow: Track the share of peak players at six to eight weeks for your ARPG, alongside units, rather than judging launch by peak alone.

lab.title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents
lab.headline: Install two skills for one job and the wrong one often runs, while the task still passes
lab.authors: Chaoliang Yan, Zihao Xu, Yuekang Li et al. (UNSW, Griffith, NTU, University of Wollongong)
lab.problem: Skills come from teams, personal folders, plugins and copied collections, and the model chooses one by name and description alone. A similar skill can replace yours and drop its key rules, such as never touching git, while completion-only evals see nothing wrong.
lab.idea: Rebuild the skills Claude Code would load in 20,947 public repos, find similar pairs, and run 312 confirmed pairs across Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 5: 6,368 runs scored on the functions only the installed skill provides.
lab.result: About 1 in 4 installed skills has a same-job twin. A twin cuts use of the installed skill by 19.9 points with no drop in task completion, and costs 9.4 points of its core functions (22.1 on Haiku, none on Opus). Replies name the skill used in 0.9% of runs. A hook blocking the twin's first read makes the model switch 96% of the time.
lab.useIt: List your personal, plugin and project skills and merge overlapping ones. Give skills distinct names and descriptions. Add a PreToolUse hook that redirects reads of known duplicate SKILL.md files, and test the rules only your skill enforces.

image.alt: Two panels: with only the project checkpoint skill the agent saves a read-only handoff; with a similar checkpoint-2 skill installed the agent commits to git without saying which skill it used

lab.title: CuACD: A Fully GPU-Resident Approximate Convex Decomposition
lab.headline: Collision hulls in a quarter second instead of 13 to 26 seconds per mesh
lab.authors: Ruoxi Shi, Xinyue Wei, Fanbo Xiang et al. (UC San Diego, Sudo GmbH)
lab.problem: Physics and collision need meshes split into convex parts. Search-based methods take tens of seconds per mesh, which pushes collision generation into overnight bakes.
lab.idea: Design the algorithm around the GPU warp: fuse the search, cutting and hull steps into kernels that stay on the GPU, with a device-side allocator so nothing round-trips to the CPU.
lab.result: Mean per mesh against CoACD at the same concavity target: 0.23 s vs 18.03 s on the V-HACD set, 0.16 s vs 12.82 s on PartNet-Mobility and 0.25 s vs 25.93 s on an Objaverse subset, with equal or better concavity and fewer parts (for example 33.6 vs 40.5).
lab.useIt: Batch-generate collision for your plugin sample meshes and ARPG props on an NVIDIA GPU, then import the convex pieces as custom collision in Unreal instead of waiting on slow decompositions.

image.alt: A gallery of meshes, from a chess piece and a Ferris wheel to a spider and a tree, each split into many colored convex parts

lab.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents
lab.headline: Plain behavior rules cut a coding agent's cost by up to 42% at the same pass rate
lab.authors: Yiran Hu, Nan Jiang, Shanchao Liang et al. (Purdue University)
lab.problem: Coding agents are expensive, and the recurring wasteful habits behind the bill had not been measured.
lab.idea: Study 1,200 SWE-bench Verified trajectories from Claude Code and Mini-SWE-Agent, name three habits (re-reading code already seen, writing near-duplicate scripts, rerunning unchanged tests), then compare three fixes over 10,000 trajectories.
lab.result: The habits appear in 79 to 98% of tasks and account for up to 22.75% of cost. A code-graph MCP raised cost in 4 of 8 settings. Agent-written skills saved at most 22.32%. Developer-written rules cut cost by 7.88 to 41.73% with pass rates within about 2.5 points.
lab.useIt: Add a short section to CLAUDE.md: state a hypothesis before searching, reuse context you already have, keep and revise one script, capture test output and rerun only when code changes, break loops. Compare cost on a few real tasks with and without it.

image.alt: An example Claude Code trajectory on a Django task marking repeated reads, near-duplicate scripts and rerun tests
